evals.prompt: Audit an unsafe read_unaligned function whose contract only guarantees len bytes. Read-only; give a concrete failure path.
evals.expected_output: Checks complete type size, initialization, pointer validity and contract.

evals.prompt: Review an unsafe impl Send for a type containing a raw pointer and interior mutability.
evals.expected_output: Traces all reachable state and required Send/Sync obligations.

evals.prompt: Audit this unsafe lock guard read-only: its unsafe impl Sync uses T: Send while the guard exposes a shared reference. Assume lock/unlock orderings are correct. Give the concrete shared-guard failure path, the narrow fix, and classify independent Relaxed counters in the same module. Do not edit.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes T:Send from T:Sync (Cell<u8> is Send but not Sync; a shared Guard exposes unsynchronized mutation); correct orderings do not fix auto-trait bounds; narrow fix is Sync requiring T:Sync; independent counters may stay Relaxed; tests do not prove soundness.

evals.prompt: Miri passes the unsafe test suite. Can I call the abstraction sound?
evals.expected_output: Explains coverage and tool limitations; no proof claim.

evals.prompt: Explain what this safe Rust iterator does. Do not assess unsafe code or safety contracts.
evals.expected_output: This is an explanation request without an unsafe-review scope.
